answer: Each agent that can claim rewards must bind its signing key to an account that has completed a human-verified, one-time stake ceremony; the registry issues a scarce credential, and contracts cap rewards per credential rather than per wallet. At dawn, rotating challenge audits can revoke credentials whose owners cannot answer consistently, so copying keys does not multiply eligibility. The anchor is the costly, rate-limited verification, not a fable that behavior alone reveals identity: an attacker must recruit more verified people and pay their time and stake.
